screens.heading: Test day
screens.body: Before the civics questions, this short lesson covers the interview itself: how the officer asks, how many answers you need right, and how to tell what kind of answer a question wants.
The civics test is a conversation. An officer asks you questions out loud. You answer out loud. There are 128 possible questions. The officer asks up to 20.
screens.alt: New citizens at a naturalization ceremony, standing close together, smiling and waving small United States flags, ceremony programmes in their hands.

screens.body: Answer 12 correctly — you pass. The officer stops as soon as you reach 12 right. If you get 9 wrong, the test ends.
Here is a real test question. Choose the answer you would give.

screens.heading: The question's opening words tell you what kind of answer
screens.body: The question's opening words tell you what kind of answer the officer wants.
Some answers change after elections — like the name of the President. This course shows today's answers and the date we checked them. Always check again before your interview.

bodyList: Stop anytime. The course remembers your place.
